walkthrough.title: Get started with Japanese Novel
walkthrough.description: Write, preview, and build a vertical-writing Japanese novel.
walkthrough.chapter.title: Write your first chapter
walkthrough.chapter.description:
Chapters are plain `.jpnov` files. Create one and start writing — ruby, emphasis dots, and page breaks are Aozora Bunko annotations, highlighted as you type. Save it with the `.jpnov` extension to collect it into a book later.
[Create a Chapter](command:workbench.action.files.newUntitledFile?%7B%22languageId%22%3A%22jpnov%22%7D)
walkthrough.preview.title: See it laid out vertically
walkthrough.preview.description:
Open the live preview to see your manuscript in vertical, right-to-left genkō-yōshi layout. It updates as you write.
[Open Preview to the Side](command:jpnov.previewToSide)
walkthrough.build.title: Collect chapters and build your book
walkthrough.build.description:
Create a Book below makes one — type a file name and the new book opens in the Books view ([open a folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder) first if needed). Add chapters, reorder them, and edit Book Info — title, running head — right there. Then check the books you want and build with the buttons at the bottom of the view: paginated HTML, an EPUB for e-readers, or Aozora-format text — the Print / Save as PDF button builds the HTML and opens it in your browser, ready to print. One `.jpbook` is one book, and it's a plain text file — hand-editing works the same.
[Create a Book](command:jpbook.createFile)
[Open the Books View](command:workbench.view.extension.jpnov)
walkthrough.highlight.title: Optional: writing and proofing aids
walkthrough.highlight.description:
Add your cast and coined words so they light up in the narration as you write — a name is coloured where it reads as the subject (`太郎は`), a keyword bolded wherever it appears. Manuscript checks — paragraph indent, sentence-ending 。, the dialogue close, and more — run as you type; each has its own switch and message in the lint settings, alongside stricter opt-in checks for submission day.
[Open Highlight Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22jpnov.editor.highlight%22)
[Open Lint Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22jpnov.lint%22)
jpnov.lint.title: Japanese Novel — Lint
jpnov.lint.common.sentenceLength.descrip: Warn when a sentence is longer than this many characters. Recommended: 100. Leave empty to disable.
jpnov.lint.common.maxTen.description: Warn when a sentence has more than this many commas (、). Recommended: 3. Leave empty to disable.
jpnov.lint.common.maxKanjiRun.descriptio: Warn when more than this many kanji appear in a row. Recommended: 6. Leave empty to disable.
jpnov.lint.common.dash.description: The dash character to use in body text. Any other dash character, or a run of an odd number of dashes, is flagged. Auto-fixable. Whichever you pick, typeset output uses the em dash (—).
jpnov.lint.common.dash.emDash.label: Em dash (—)
jpnov.lint.common.dash.boxDrawing.label: Box drawing (─)
jpnov.lint.common.ellipsis.description: Flag an odd-count run of the ellipsis (… or ‥), and 。。 / 、、 / ・・ runs standing in for one. Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.common.exclamationSpace.descr: Require a full-width space after ！ / ？ when text continues on the line. Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.common.exclamationRun.descrip: Keep ！？ in shape for vertical text: a lone mark should be full-width, a double should be the half-width pair (!? sits in one square via 縦中横), and three or more in a row are flagged. Singles and doubles are auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.common.arabicDigits.descripti: Warn when an Arabic-numeral run is longer than this many digits. Recommended: 2. Leave empty to disable.
jpnov.lint.common.noTrailingSpace.descri: Flag spaces (full- or half-width) or tabs at the end of a line. A line of nothing but spaces counts too. A line ending in an annotation such as ［＃字下げ］ is left alone. Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.common.blankRun.description: Warn when more than this many blank lines appear in a row. Use 0 to forbid them. Recommended: 1. Leave empty to disable. Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.common.noHankakuKana.descript: Flag half-width kana and half-width punctuation / brackets (ｱ, ｲ, ｡, ｢｣ …).
jpnov.lint.common.noNfd.description: Flag decomposed (NFD) characters; prefer the composed (NFC) form.
jpnov.lint.common.shiftJisSafe.descripti: Flag characters Shift JIS lacks. The check runs no matter which encoding you build with, so a manuscript stays ready for a Shift JIS submission. Covers annotations and ruby as well as body text.
jpnov.lint.common.jaNoSpaceBetweenFullWi: Flag a half-width space between two full-width characters. Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.common.jaUnnaturalAlphabet.de: Flag a lone letter, half- or full-width, caught between Japanese characters (見るr — a letter the IME left unconverted). Vowels, n, and capital letters are left alone.
jpnov.lint.common.minusPosition.descript: Flag a minus sign that is not directly before a number. A Western hyphen between letters (Wi-Fi) is left alone.
jpnov.lint.narration.indent.description: Require a narration line to start with a full-width space (　) or an opening bracket; a ［＃字下げ］ annotation also counts, and headings and ornament-only lines (a ＊ scene break) are exempt — a bare …… line is narration. Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.narration.endPeriod.descripti: Flag a narration line that does not end with 。 (！？ and closing quotes are allowed; a trailing … or dash still wants its 。). Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.dialogue.closingPunct.descrip: Flag 。 / 、 right before a closing bracket (」』) — dialogue ends without a period. Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.dialogue.noIndent.description: Flag a dialogue line that starts with a full-width space before its 「. Auto-fixable.
jpnov.lint.ruby.kana.description: Require every ruby reading 《…》 to be all one kana type (this also rejects half-width kana and NFD).
jpnov.lint.ruby.kana.off.label: Off
jpnov.lint.ruby.kana.off.description: No kana-type check on ruby readings.
jpnov.lint.ruby.kana.hiragana.label: All hiragana
jpnov.lint.ruby.kana.hiragana.descriptio: Every reading must be hiragana only.
jpnov.lint.ruby.kana.katakana.label: All katakana
jpnov.lint.ruby.kana.katakana.descriptio: Every reading must be katakana only.
jpnov.layout.title: Japanese Novel — Layout & Output
jpnov.layout.charsPerLine.description: Characters per line for the preview and the HTML build grid.
jpnov.layout.linesPerPage.description: Lines per page for the HTML build grid. The preview scrolls continuously; with ruled lines turned on, it frames this many lines as one page.
jpnov.layout.linePitch.description: The distance from the center of one line to the center of the next, as a multiple of the character size. Applies to the preview and the built HTML.
jpnov.layout.linePitch.1.5.description: The tightest pitch. Ruby readings sit flush against the neighbouring line.
jpnov.layout.linePitch.1.75.description: A tight pitch. Ruby readings stay just clear of the neighbouring line.
jpnov.layout.linePitch.2.description: A full character of space between lines. Ruby readings fit exactly, even with ruled lines drawn or left ruby added.
jpnov.layout.linePitch.2.25.description: Extra room between lines. Ruled lines stay clear of ruby readings.
jpnov.layout.fontFamily.description: The body font, as a CSS font-family list (for example: "Yu Mincho", serif). Applies to both the preview and the built HTML. Leave empty to use a built-in Mincho stack.
jpnov.layout.kinsoku.description: Japanese line-breaking rules: keep forbidden characters off line starts and ends, never split ―― or ……, and hang a trailing 、。 into the margin. Applies to both the preview and the built book.
jpnov.layout.kinsoku.none.label: Off
jpnov.layout.kinsoku.none.description: No line-breaking rules — bare wrap at the column width.
jpnov.layout.kinsoku.relaxed.label: Relaxed
jpnov.layout.kinsoku.relaxed.description: Closing brackets, punctuation, middle dots (・：；) and repetition marks (々ゝゞヽヾ〻) never start a line; small kana and ー may. Same as Word's standard level.
jpnov.layout.kinsoku.strict.label: Strict
jpnov.layout.kinsoku.strict.description: Everything in Relaxed, plus small kana and ー never start a line, and a run of ―― or …… stays together as one unit. Same as Word's high level.
jpnov.layout.autoTcy.description: Automatically set half-width punctuation pairs upright in one square (tate-chū-yoko / 縦中横). Manual ［＃縦中横］…［＃縦中横終わり］ always applies. Reflected in the preview and every built book; the text build writes explicit markers. Use full-width marks where a pair should stay as typed.
jpnov.layout.autoTcy.none.label: Off
jpnov.layout.autoTcy.none.description: Half-width pairs stay as typed, lying on their side.
jpnov.layout.autoTcy.punctuationPairs.de: A pair of half-width ! / ? stands upright in one square.
jpnov.layout.preview.lineNumbers.descrip: Show a small line number at the head of each line in the preview.
jpnov.layout.preview.edgeLine.descriptio: Draw a ruled line between text lines in the preview.
jpnov.layout.preview.edgeLine.none.label: None
jpnov.layout.preview.edgeLine.text.label: Text colour
jpnov.layout.preview.edgeLine.text.descr: Ruled lines in the text colour.
jpnov.layout.preview.edgeLine.red.label: Red
jpnov.layout.preview.edgeLine.red.descri: Red ruled lines, like classic manuscript paper.
jpnov.layout.paper.size.description: Paper size of the built HTML — the pages print at this size. The page grid keeps its character and line counts and scales to fit the paper, centred.
jpnov.layout.paper.size.a4.label: A4
jpnov.layout.paper.size.a6.label: A6
jpnov.layout.paper.size.a6.description: 105 × 148 mm, about the size of a Japanese bunko paperback.
jpnov.layout.paper.orientation.descripti: Paper orientation of the built HTML. Auto matches the shape of the page grid.
jpnov.layout.paper.orientation.auto.desc: Landscape when the page grid is wide, portrait when it is tall.
jpnov.layout.paper.lineNumbers.descripti: Show a small line number at the head of each line in the built HTML.
jpnov.layout.paper.edgeLine.description: Draw a ruled line between text lines and a matching border around each page in the built HTML.
jpnov.layout.paper.edgeLine.none.label: None
jpnov.layout.paper.edgeLine.text.label: Text colour
jpnov.layout.paper.edgeLine.text.descrip: Ruled lines in the text colour.
jpnov.layout.paper.edgeLine.red.label: Red
jpnov.layout.paper.edgeLine.red.descript: Red ruled lines, like classic manuscript paper.
jpnov.layout.txt.encoding.description: Encoding of the built `.txt` book. Characters the encoding lacks are written as 〓, and the build reports how many.
jpnov.layout.txt.encoding.shiftJis.label: Shift JIS
jpnov.layout.txt.encoding.shiftJis.descr: The encoding of Aozora Bunko texts. Turn on `files.autoGuessEncoding` and VS Code opens the built file with the right encoding.
jpnov.layout.txt.encoding.utf8.label: UTF-8
jpnov.layout.txt.encoding.utf8.descripti: Every character is written as typed.
jpnov.layout.txt.encoding.utf8Bom.label: UTF-8 with BOM
jpnov.layout.txt.encoding.utf8Bom.descri: UTF-8 with a byte order mark at the start. Windows apps open it as UTF-8.
jpnov.layout.outDir.description: Folder (relative to the workspace folder) where built `.html` / `.epub` / `.txt` books are written. Files inside it are never picked up as books.
jpnov.editor.updateRefsOnFileMove.descri: When a chapter file or folder is renamed or moved inside VS Code, update the paths listed in the workspace's book files (`.jpbook`). A path that no longer resolves is flagged in the editor.
jpnov.editor.title: Japanese Novel — Editor
jpnov.editor.autoIndent.description: Start each new line with a full-width space on Enter. The space is removed again when you open the line with 「 or 『, or press Enter without adding anything. Only automatically inserted spaces are removed.
jpnov.editor.highlight.characters.descri: Your cast, one name per item (e.g. `山田　太郎`). A name splits on the space into surname + given, so the full name, the surname, and the given name are each recognised. Highlighted in narration where it reads as a subject — the name (one honorific such as `さん` / `先生` allowed) directly followed by `は` or `が`. Empty and duplicate items are ignored.
jpnov.editor.highlight.keywords.descript: Coined terms — a fantasy noun, a place name, … — one per item. Bolded in narration, in the ordinary text colour. Where a term is also a character name, the subject form (followed by `は` / `が`) counts as the character and every other occurrence as a keyword. Empty and duplicate items are ignored.
